_readme: Which optional data bundles are actually shipped, and why any of them is not. This file is COMMITTED and always present; the app reads it before reaching for a bundle, so a deliberately-absent file is answered from data rather than from a 404. That matters twice: the console stays clean (acceptance criterion 1 is 'no console errors', and a 404 is a console error even when it is expected), and BITE can print a sentence somebody wrote on purpose instead of an HTTP status. Each entry carries a SHORT reason, which is what an instrument flag shows, and a longer detail, which is what the BITE page adds underneath it. scripts/build-navdata.mjs rewrites the navdata entry when it emits the bundle.

navdata.reason: navdata bundle not generated — not needed by any v1 panel
navdata.detail: The airport, runway and navaid database backs the HSI and nav pages, which are v2 and gated behind the attitude stability test. Nothing on the PFD, ATIS or BITE pages reads it, so its absence costs nothing on screen. It is also not generated because OurAirports' published terms at ourairports.com/data/ are not reachable from the build sandbox and have not been read; the data itself IS reachable. Run `npm run navdata` once the terms are read, or `node scripts/build-navdata.mjs --from <dir>` with the three CSVs.

geoid.detail: EGM96 geoid heights over the region, 17x21 at 0.25 degrees, -37.83 to -21.22 m. NGA/NASA, public domain.

wmm.detail: World Magnetic Model 2025, degree 12, valid 2024-11-13T03:00:00.000Z to 2029-11-13T03:00:00.000Z. NOAA NCEI and BGS.
